<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Circle</title>
  <style>
    *,
    *::before,
    *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }

    html,
    body {
      height: 100%;
    }

    body {
      min-height: 100vh;
      display: flex;
      justify-content: center;
      align-items: center;
      background: #f5f5f5;
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    svg {
      width: min(400px, 80vw);
      height: auto;
      display: block;
    }

    circle {
      fill: #1e293b;
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <svg id="ae683f770" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="circle-title">
    <title id="circle-title">A filled circle</title>
    <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200"/>
  </svg>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
Updated `0.html` with these improvements:

- **No horizontal scrollbar.** Replaced `width: 100vw` with a full-height body and `min-height`, which avoids the scrollbar width overflow.
- **Responsive SVG.** The circle now scales down on narrow screens instead of staying fixed at a size that could overflow small viewports.
- **Accessibility.** Added `role="img"` and an SVG title so screen readers announce the graphic instead of skipping it.
- **Visible styling.** Gave the circle an explicit fill and the page a light background so the shape stands out, and added `box-sizing: border-box` to the reset.
- **Readable title.** Changed the tab title from a hash string to "Circle".

The circle itself is unchanged in geometry. Open the file in a browser to confirm the layout.
